title: Staged invoice escrow
kicker: Pay part. Keep the remainder visible.
summary: Follow one payment through seller receipt, the source fee, and the duties left in escrow.
utility: Explain exactly what the buyer funds, what the seller receives, and what is still owed.

strands.label: Payment arithmetic
strands.claim: The seller payment matches the chosen partial amount.
strands.statement: Opening invoice duty 100 CASH; payment 35 CASH; escrow debit for payment and fee 37 CASH.
strands.authentication: The worksheet supplies an illustrative opening state; an application would need its actual predecessor and exact CASH identity.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Fee accounting
strands.claim: The 2 CASH source fee is a separate payment.
strands.statement: Escrow pays seller 35 CASH and fees 2 CASH; the fee does not discharge invoice duty.
strands.authentication: Source S12 names escrow, seller, fees, and CASH; actual outputs still need the consuming validator.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Duty continuation
strands.claim: Partial payment preserves the unpaid invoice and reserve duty.
strands.statement: Invoice 100 − 35 = 65 CASH; reserve duty remains 10 CASH; total duties 75 CASH.
strands.authentication: The starting duty amounts are worksheet premises; a real application must bind them to its predecessor.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

effects: Source-funded cash 110 − payment 35 − fee 2 = 73 CASH; duties total 75 CASH, a backing gap of 2 CASH.
Proposed extra funding gives cash 112 − 35 − 2 = 75 CASH, matching duties for this one partial.
The source partial action requires 0 < amount < opening invoice duty. Paying the whole invoice uses finish(), which has different fee behavior.
dependencies: These are future proof roles, not three existing proof producers.
Funding 112 is a proposed backing policy; S12 contains no extra-funding action.
Every further partial charges another 2 CASH. One extra fee budget does not fund a sequence of partials.
The source has no reserve-duty-return action. Staged delivery and recovery need additional implementation.

title: Batched DEX orders
kicker: Give every order its own outcome.
summary: Connect each order’s exact assets and minimum net receipt to a specified pool transition.
utility: Let a batch builder explain each owner’s result alongside the shared pool arithmetic.

strands.label: Order arithmetic
strands.claim: Each illustrated order meets its own amount bounds.
strands.statement: Two orders each offer 100 A and require at least 90 B net; the illustration assigns each owner 92 B.
strands.authentication: Exact asset identities, owner limits, and actual outputs must be supplied and bound by a real application.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Pool arithmetic
strands.claim: A supported pool relation explains the pool continuation.
strands.statement: The chosen reserve update, fee rule, and exact rounding must agree with the two illustrated orders.
strands.authentication: No pool reserve or price observation is supplied here; pool state provenance remains a required input.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate. No pool computation or verified price is shown.

strands.label: Batch accounting
strands.claim: Order and pool amounts agree across the batch.
strands.statement: The same amounts used for each owner’s result must appear in the batch accounting.
strands.authentication: Actual output allocation belongs to the consuming validator under its selected profile.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate. The strict illustration uses a separate output per order; coalesced-payment partition is a separate policy choice.

effects: Each illustrated owner gives 100 A and receives 92 B net against a minimum of 90 B.
Pool balances, fees, and rounding need a complete independent worksheet before execution.
A partial fill must retain unfilled quantity and duties; cancellation is a separate action.
dependencies: Identify supported order and pool relations and their actual proof producers.
Choose and enforce actual-output allocation for the consumer’s profile.
Supply exact asset, recipient, fee, rounding, continuation, and cancellation rules.

title: Capped issuance
kicker: Show where every issued unit goes.
summary: Keep application-asset supply, recipient distribution, and any servicing promises distinct.
utility: Give an issuer an inspectable account of new supply and the obligations attached to it.

strands.label: Supply arithmetic
strands.claim: The proposed supply update stays within the cap.
strands.statement: Illustrative first issue: 300 application-asset units under a cap of 1,000; unissued capacity is 700.
strands.authentication: The issuer policy, exact application asset, and supply predecessor need an actual authenticated path.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Distribution arithmetic
strands.claim: The recipient allocation totals the issued amount.
strands.statement: Recipient one receives 180 units and recipient two receives 120 units; 180 + 120 = 300.
strands.authentication: Recipient identities and actual mint and payment outputs must be enforced by the applicable policies and validators.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Duty accounting
strands.claim: Servicing duties remain separate from token supply.
strands.statement: The remaining 700 units of issue capacity are not debt. A redemption promise is a duty only when explicitly defined.
strands.authentication: Any servicing promise needs named parties, an exact asset, and a defined creation and discharge rule.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate. This illustration supplies no redemption agreement.

effects: Application-asset issuance is 300 units: 180 to one recipient and 120 to the other.
Unissued capacity is 700 units, with no debt inferred from that capacity.
Issuing a proof claim token does not mint the application asset.
dependencies: Implement supported application mint/burn semantics and actual mint-policy enforcement.
Continue supply state and bind exact recipients and assets.
Define any separate redemption duty; external eligibility documents retain their issuer and freshness assumptions.

title: Loan servicing
summary: Show principal, accrual, payment, fee, and remaining debt as different amounts.
utility: Help borrower and lender inspect how a payment changes the outstanding duty.

strands.label: Accrual arithmetic
strands.claim: The defined period’s accrual updates opening debt.
strands.statement: Illustrative debt 100 CASH plus accrual 5 CASH gives a duty of 105 CASH.
strands.authentication: The agreement must supply the period, rate, rounding, and provenance of any variable-rate observation.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate. No rate source or live accrual is supplied.

strands.label: Payment accounting
strands.claim: Payment and fee retain their different meanings.
strands.statement: Debt payment 35 CASH plus separate fee 2 CASH gives payer gross debit 37 CASH.
strands.authentication: The actual payer, lender, fee recipient, and exact asset must agree with owner authorization and transaction effects.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Debt continuation
strands.claim: Only the payment discharges the debt.
strands.statement: Duty 105 − repayment 35 = 70 CASH remaining; the fee 2 is not repayment.
strands.authentication: A real continuation must bind the predecessor duty and its explicit accrual and discharge entries.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

effects: Payer gross debit is 37 CASH: repayment 35 and fee 2.
Closing debt is 70 CASH. Collateral release requires its own policy.
dependencies: Define period, rate, rounding, and any observation freshness rule.
Bind actual loan payments and the continuing debt to the authorized transition.
Supply separate origination and collateral policies; this lesson establishes no ACTUS conformance.

title: Treasury allocation
kicker: Follow the amounts into the reserve.
summary: Separate allocation arithmetic, actual transfers, and the duties that remain afterward.
utility: Make the beneficiary amounts, fee budget, and reserve or rebate duties visible to owners.

strands.label: Quotient arithmetic
strands.claim: The allocation inputs satisfy the source arithmetic.
strands.statement: For allocate(true,23,7,2): 23 = 3 × 7 + 2 and 2 < 3. The units input is checked, not debited.
strands.authentication: The approved input is a supplied parameter in S13; separate governance authentication remains a dependency.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Transfer accounting
strands.claim: The allocation amounts match the quotient.
strands.statement: Alpha receives 14 A and 4 B; beta receives 7 A; fees receive 2 A. Total custody debit is 23 A and 4 B.
strands.authentication: Actual vault custody, exact A and B identities, recipient outputs, and owner authorization need the consuming profile.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate.

strands.label: Reserve accounting
strands.claim: New duties remain explicit after allocation.
strands.statement: Create allocation reserve duty 2 A and rebate duty 6 B. Proposed backing 25 A / 10 B leaves cash 2 A / 6 B.
strands.authentication: Opening custody is an explicit premise; proposed full backing needs a consumer-enforced policy.
strands.limits: Illustrative requirement only: no concrete proof instance or independent producer is supplied. These arithmetic checks may share one whole-execution proof. Actual signatures and validator enforcement remain separate. Source minimum custody is 23 A / 4 B; backing is a separate policy.

effects: Source custody minimum for this step: 23 A and 4 B.
Proposed full backing: begin with 25 A and 10 B to retain 2 A and 6 B after the step.
The allocation creates duties of 2 A and 6 B; it does not discharge them.
rebate(amount) can discharge the B rebate. S13 has no allocation_reserve discharge action.
dependencies: Give a distinct governance decision its named authentication path where the policy requires one.
Bind actual beneficiaries, fees, custody, and the continuing reserve duties.
Full backing is proposed application policy, beyond source non-negative custody.
A reserve-duty discharge or migration requires additional program work.
